utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I hear a lot of a language that I cannot understand on channel four, so there must be some technical problem. Could we just see -- now I hear only my own voice, which is certainly not more pleasant than what I heard before, but it's English now. On five we now have French, and I do understand that we have B/C/S on six. So everything is now as it should be. Madam Registrar, could you again call the case in a language I understand.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before the Prosecution continues to cross-examine the witness, I was wondering, the Chamber was wondering whether we would get any additional information about maps. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We met with the Defence yesterday. I anticipate that I will be in a position to give you some more information and an example at 11.00, if that is convenient to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are anxious to hear at 11.00 what news there is about maps. Then we could continue with the cross-examination of the witness. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP18.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration that you have given at the beginning of your testimony. Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would ask with the assistance of the usher that the witness be shown once again the large coloured map. That would be map C2, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday when we took the recess we were focussing our attention on the feature on the map marked as Obeljak, do you see that on the map, and if you do can you please point to it with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that feature according to the map has an elevation of 1180 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could please --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could please look to the north-east of Obeljak, approximately 3 centimetres you'll see a feature marked as Golo Brdo or Golo BR. Do you see that on the map and can you please point to it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That feature, according to the map, has an elevation of 1246 metres; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And finally, Witness, if you could look in a north northerly direction slightly to the east of Golo Brdo, past the word "Lukva" do you see another feature mark would an elevation of 1063 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I've asked you to draw to the Trial Chamber's attention what is basically an arc of elevated hills from the Grivici area through this hill that we just marked near Lukva. Can you please trace the line on the map with the pointer of the hills that we spoke about.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. During the period that you've testified about, that is 1992 through 1994, these hills were under the control of the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At what point in time did the VRS come to control these hills?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the end of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And from the end of July 1993 through the period at least to include August 1994, the VRS maintained control of this arc of high ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And in effect, Witness, the area of Hadzici and its surroundings settlements and villages compared the high ground that you've just indicated was at a lower elevation; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday you told us that you saw on the ABiH side two T-34 tanks; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall testifying that the range of that weapon system is 18.000 to 20.000 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I suggest to you that the effective range of the T-34 tank is more along the lines of 900 to 1.000 metres. What is your response to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During the course, Witness, of your military training in either in the JNA or your military experience with the VRS, on how many occasions did you personally train on the T-34 tank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have a number of questions that stem from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, first of all, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were asked about the moment when the VRS took control of the elevations in the surrounding area of the sector that we were talking about, the urban sector we were talking about. My question is the following: At the time that you mentioned, and I believe that was summer, that is July of 1993, which battle took place at the time when these elevations were taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were battles for Obeljak, Stupnik and Golo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And when you are talking about the fighting, what can you say in relation to their importance and what I mean by that is what was the intensity of the exchange of fire? How long did the fighting last? What was its duration and so on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was for one day, day and a half, that's how long the fighting lasted for these elevations.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What type of exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was infantry and artillery fire on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now I'd like to come back to the question of the tanks, the T-34 tanks. A question of the Prosecution and you said that you never said any training on the T-34, and my question is the following: Were you, however, in contact during either your military service or during the war, were you in contact with weapons like tanks, for instance, T-34s? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With T-55, yes, but not with T-34.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. My question is the following: You said that your weapons were often targeted by the weapons of the opposing side, the army of the opposing side. And when you are speaking about the range of these weapons, did you receive precise instructions regarding the protection of your own weapons in relation to the tanks that could be active?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My crew was at about 2.000 metres away from that tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And were you able to -- or I'll rephrase. You still able to be a target for this tank at that distance?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President. That is a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you please refrain from leading, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you said -- I'll rephrase the question. Were you ever the target of firing from a tank during the period of the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, that is also a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When your unit was targeted, do you know by what weapons you were targeted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as the tank T-35 [as interpreted] is concerned, my crew wasn't targeted personally, wasn't because we were sheltered, we sheltered ourselves, but it did target other -- our colleagues, our fellow combatants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you see that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where at that very moment was this tank, and I now hear T-35, was located exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] T-34.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It must be then an error in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was on the Borak hill, on the Borak hill.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and that was at approximately what distance from your positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] About 2.000 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were exactly where located at that moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From our tank position -- from the tank position -- sorry, on the Kopisanj hill above Hadzici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you see it with binoculars or with the naked eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was possible with the naked eye, but it was better to see the type of the tank with the binoculars because it wasn't such a long distance, particularly the infantry from the bunkers were able to see it with a naked eye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about fighting with infantry weapons, do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you be more specific as to what were the infantry weapons used?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Objection, Mr. President, these questions do not arise out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Present, I have simply -- I am simply asking the questions around tanks, but throughout the time the witness answering said that there was fighting of artillery and infantry weapons when these elevations were taken or retaken in 1993. In a sense that he is speaking about fighting, about the infantry and infantry weapons, I believe that it is the right, absolute right of the Defence to continue to question on this point so that we know where did the firing go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, as far as my recollection goes, the Prosecution asked when the hills were taken, and I think that you asked for further details in respect of the battle during which the -- during which the hills were retaken by the forces of which the -- in which the witness participated. So it does not arise out of cross-examination. One question would not be, but it should not be something really an issue that should be dealt with more extensively. So if you had more questions in mind, I would like to ask you to move to your next subject, and if it is just one or two questions, and I really mean one or two questions, then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It won't be necessary, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means no further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's what I meant, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that you said "ce n'est pas la peine" and it was not immediately clear to me that that meant that you had no further questions. Judge Nieto-Navia has one or more questions to you, Mr. DP18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Might the witness be shown the coloured map, please. With the pointer would you please point to your positions on that map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: My unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Now, would you please point to the positions of the tank or of the tanks.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is this hill, Kopisanj here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Please point to both positions again.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: That's the first one.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is -- it is a very small area here, so it will be this small circle here where this plateau was. Approximately, the plateau was about 3 to 400 metres large.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: That was when? Which is the date of the -- the date in which the BH Army was there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not here. These were our positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Please, point to the positions where the tanks were, the tanks, the BH Army tanks were.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP18 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: That's different, yes. Thank you. No more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since Judge El Mahdi and myself have no further questions for you, this concludes your testimony in this court. Mr. DP18, I thank you very much for coming the very long way to The Hague and for answering all the questions of both parties and of the Bench and I wish you a safe trip home again. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, can you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Far from me for wanting to interrupt whatsoever, but it could happen that the witness arrives somewhat belatedly, because the instructions that we gave to the competent unit was based on the fact that we thought that the Prosecution would continue for longer with the cross-examination. So if this is the case, if the witness comes late, we apologise, but we didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We will first try to find out where the witness is. But before doing so, perhaps we first deal with the documents in respect of the Witness DP18. Madam Registrar. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1807, under seal, pseudonym sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That document is admitted in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The witness has not yet arrived, but is expected to arrive in a couple of minutes. Before we continue, I'd first like to go into closed session -- private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I make it clear to both you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, and to the Prosecution that the Chamber would certainly welcome whatever proposal to have maps where the parties could agree upon. From your beginning I take it that you have not reached such an agreement. Under these circumstances, the Chamber would prefer to first listen to a party that comes with a proposal, then hears the possible objection of the other party, and not spend too much time on that. Because the Chamber has received a lot of maps with or without objections, and finally, if the parties cannot agree upon maps, then the Chamber will have to do it with the maps that are tendered in evidence and are admitted into evidence. And it's -- we could go on until January, February or March to discuss maps. The Chamber, as I said before, would certainly welcome whatever shared proposal by the parties, and otherwise the Chamber will hear what the parties are offering, the Chamber will hear the objections and will give a decision. That will be the following order. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. If I may simply indicate what I wanted to say. My objection is of a strictly methodological nature. We object first of all for the following reason: The maps that the Prosecution wanted to tender a moment ago, are maps that include new information, this is not cartographic information at all, it is technical information which has nothing to do with the geography or cartography and which would tend to introduce new information for your Chamber which was never submitted to the Defence on the one side, and on the other never to the witnesses. Therefore, as far as the map itself is concerned to show it to your Chamber as such would imply something that is not admissible because it would be like tendering exhibits with additional information that was never communicated to the Defence within the frameworks prescribed by the Rules. And in that way one would, undercover, to put it that way, introduce information that we don't need and as such, this is not acceptable. And that is the reason that we formulated our objection above all for methodological reasons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are telling us what is on the map that has not been proposed to us. So in order to understand your objection, I would and this Chamber would stick to the order, that is also a matter of methodology, and that you first see what is proposed and better understand what your objections are because we have no idea what will be on those maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We heard what you said before I said it. The following order would be if one of the parties comes up with whatever maps, we will see what it is we will hear the objections and then we will then decide.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would request from your Chamber - I am sorry - that it render a decision to the effect that if a map of whatever kind needs to be tendered -- is to be tendered by the Prosecution, that it should not contain other information or indication than information contained in other prior documents. And certainly not tendentious additional information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will give a decision when the map has been tendered when we have heard the parties about it. A general decision on what kind of maps could and under whatever circumstances would be admitted would not be a decision that the Chamber will take at this very moment. Is there anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am taking steps at the moment via email to have the maps, that is the samples brought down to court immediately. It may well be that I could start my submissions in a matter of a minute or so. It may be in two parts. There may be some further documents available by 11.00, but at least we could take advantage of the available time to commence that procedure, if those maps arrive in the next minute or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will wait one or two minutes, and if not we will have a short break. Let's see what happens during the next two minutes. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I hand up some copies of a document and provide one to the Defence as well. I trust that five will be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- At this stage I would like to rephrase a formulation. That was not the map that we saw when we had our discussion. I fully understand the embarrassment of the Prosecution, but this is not that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this is exactly the reason, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, why the Chamber prefers first to see what maps are offered and then hear any objections to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I respond to that? I specifically said to Mr. Piletta-Zanin yesterday that the map I handed him then would not be the map that I would hand to the Trial Chamber this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it was time available anyhow these few minutes. So let's restart about the maps. Please proceed, Mr. -- Unless the witness is already -- the witness has arrived. Perhaps you -- perhaps we start with the maps so that we --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Mr. President. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- We know at least what we have to think about in the near future.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Office of the Prosecutor has received some new software on the 6th of November 2002 which enables our mapping people to produce a different map on the same information as is contained in the sniping and shelling scheduled incident maps with a projection that enables the use of a ruler to determine with precision the distance between any two spots on the map. Secondly, we are now able to produce maps with more visible contours. This software was very expensive. I understand it to be in the order of many thousands of dollars for one license alone. What I have handed up is an example based on incidents 3 and 8 because evidence in the last week or so has particularly focused on the part of Sarajevo which concerns those two incidents. Mr. President, there are now on this sample, two ways of measuring distances between any two spots regardless of whether the line between the two spots is horizontal, vertical or diagonal. That is, by referring to the 100 metre delineation points on the horizontal and vertical axis, that is the latitudinal and longitudinal lines, alternatively by using the scale which appears at the bottom of the map. In producing this projection, objects on the original maps are elongated and so the circles indicating the suspected source of fire become oval shaped. The black depictions of buildings become in some cases perhaps longer or shorter. I emphasise that the change in shape of those symbols does not effect lines of sight. Mr. President, this software enables other steps to be taken in relation to the same information. I do not propose at this stage to tender that material unless the Trial Chamber wishes to understand more about it. It may indeed well be that in case in rebuttal by the Prosecution that we produce further maps, as a response to issues raised for the first time by the Defence in the Defence case. Mr. President, the software enables one to determine lines of sight, in other words, to produce a -- it can be done in different ways, firstly by producing a 3-D image of the topography, and then manipulating that 3-D image on the screen. By the word "manipulation" I mean simply turning it around so that it can be observed from different angles. Secondly, lines of sight can be determined on this two-dimensional depiction. In this particular example there are changes in the colours of the lines of sight between green and red. Red indicates portions along that line of sight that could not be seen. That depiction, of course, assumes, has to make assumptions as to how high, if at all, above the ground level the eyes are at the suspected source of fire. It makes no allowance for vegetation. One can factor in a height at the suspected source of fire, if, for instance, one assumes the person is standing or wishes to see what the line of sight would be if a person was standing, one could factor into the software a height for argument's sake 1 3/4 metres and then see what line of sight is produced. Mr. President, at a later point, at 11.00, I will hand up an example of that 3-D image, but I emphasise the purpose in doing so is simply to acquaint the Trial Chamber the parameters of this new software in terms of what is possible and what is not. Can I just add this: I am concerned that in tendering these maps, if the tender is accepted, we will not have the benefit of changes made to the, for instance, to the confrontation lines by a number of witnesses in the -- some in the Prosecution case, most in the Defence case. I respectfully submit that the purpose to which these new maps could be put is if one regards the maps already tendered as the primary exhibit, but wishes to supplement that exhibit with information as to the precise distances between two points, one could identify the two relevant points of the maps already tendered, then go to these maps, locate the same two points, and then make a measurement with confidence. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I give an opportunity to Mr. Piletta-Zanin to answer, I would have two questions, Mr. Ierace. The first one would be, is it possible on these maps to take out the confrontation lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. As I understand it, it is. I can confirm that by 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that would mean that the -- what is on the map then would just be, as you say, lines of sight, at least lines between two different points. Then my next question would be: What is the basis for the measuring of the height, because I see on these maps there are lines that indicate that what elevation these lines are. Usually they go, I take it from 50 metres, 50 metres up, 50 metres down. But, of course, if I am in a position behind a rock of 12 metres high --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I see would nothing as far as the lines on the map are concerned, but nevertheless the rock could take my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain to me how these I would say minor details in the terrain are dealt with by this system?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. As I understand it, the buildings are incorporated so that if a building blocks a line of sight, that is, a building which appears on the map symbolised, then that is taken into account. The number of contours can be adjusted on the maps so that one could see a large number of contours at a shorter distance in altitude. I will give precise answers to those questions at 11.00, if that is convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but would these contours also include natural features? I do understand that vegetation is not among them, but, for example, the example I just gave, behind the rock of 10 meters high.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I would need to consult with the map people to answer that question. Rather than indicate what I suspect to be a situation, I prefer to consult first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, no final answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: I have a question. I have this map. This map is the former map on the sniping incident number 3, the one that we had before. The new one is taken from this one or from the original of this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: In a manner of speaking, Your Honour, the information which was used to produce the earlier maps is used to produce this map with a different projection, and in this particular case, indicating what could be seen along those two lines of sight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: My question is because the confrontation lines are not the same, as far as I can see. There is a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Excuse me a minute, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To give you an example, the confrontation lines in the area we are talking about never come as close as on this draft, on the left-hand side of the draft, close to the 3 and 8 points. I never saw them so close to each other and certainly not on the other map.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, I will check that, Mr. President and Your Honour, and I will respond to that at 11.00 if that is convenient.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Mr. Ierace, could I ask you a question, please. I was wondering about the map which is the original for all these maps. Whom did it -- who published it, who made it, on what date, and is it the only one available or rather several maps of the region?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I understand that the satellite imaging which is entered into the software and which provides the topographical information was recorded around 1997, 19 -- somewhere between 1996 and 1997. The other detail which appears in the maps such as streets and so on, I understand comes from a map which was produced immediately following Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the war. Again, I will check that precise information by 11.00. Does that answer your question, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you very much. But I would also have a question to put to Mr. Piletta-Zanin. I, of course, if the President allows me. I am at your service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you think it is more useful to ask Mr. Piletta-Zanin your question before I give him the chance to react or whichever you prefer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it hasn't got to do with these maps, it has to do with the origins of the maps tendered by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also have some questions about that. I would suggest that we give the floor to Mr. Piletta-Zanin to react first and as we have additional questions we could put them to him after his response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As you wish, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with the assistance of Madam Usher, I should like to place a document on the ELMO that we received from the Prosecution. I am doing it because we only have one copy and in that way we can all see it, if I have your permission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. What I am asking you as a question is the origins of your map --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry, I thought that question would come later. Which map are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The map of the army, the large military map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The C2, I see. I am going to consult with my colleague and ask him -- when you mean "origin," you mean you wish to know who published it, the same question addressed to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, who and how and as regards the authenticity as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for your question, Your Honour. The answer that we can give you at present is the following: It appears, but I underline, it appears that these maps are of the General Staff maps, which mean that they were produced by the General Staff machinery, on what technical basis I can't tell you now, and we will consider that matter and see what other purely technical information we can provide you with regarding the date the map was produced, for instance, then the scientific entity, that is, the author of the map, et cetera, but this is information I am unable to give you offhand now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE EL MAHDI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with the assistance of Madam Usher, could you please place on the ELMO this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know where the colour can be seen well on this reproduction, Mr. President, but we can see very well on this document that represents the same zone as the other map. We can see very well that on this map the red line is far longer than the green line, and I would be grateful to the usher if she could point with her finger the end of the red line, please because we will see it better if you point it out to us. Thank you very much. And the other line. Thank you. So it is now clear for everyone --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I'd like to ask the usher to zoom in on the circles on the top because on the screen I see a totally different colour, and I do not see the numbers 3 and 8 appear. So I am not quite sure that we are looking to the same map as has been handed out to us. Could we please see -- I see some two blue ovals at the left top corner without any numbers in it, whereas I received a document which says "draft" and which has two red ovals with the numbers 3 and 8 in it. So, therefore, I would very much like to know that everyone has been handed out the same -- I am just -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have here a map of the same area. We can recognise the same hills to the right. They were -- this is the map tendered by the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. On the right there are orchards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And they concern the same incidents, that is incidents 3 and 8, which can be seen at the bottom of the map, and we will see that later. What we see is that the red lines in this first version are much, considerably longer than the red lines in the other document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Prosecution gives another map, and to tell the Chamber that you could produce -- that they have handed out to you yesterday other maps, the Chamber has to concentrate on what it is presented with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that if I ask whether the confrontation lines could be taken out, I take it that you could change whatever you would like to change in this map. So that the -- I think the Chamber is fully aware that changing the data, changing the colours, changing the lines, that you could produce many maps, and the Chamber will have to consider whether the map presented by the Prosecution or a map presented by the Defence would be an acceptable document to work with. So there is, at this moment, as far as I am concerned, I can't imagine that you would even move the orchards on maps so there is no need to explain on these kinds of documents you could easily change things -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, what I want to say is that there is a considerable difference between the methodology used before and the methodology used now. Because before we only had the theoretical line, theoretical line of fire, that's it. Now, today, what we are being proposed is the result of brand new software that would enable us not to have the theoretical line, but the witness or the person there would have seen. So what is happening is the Prosecution, they can enlarge that red area as much as they like, and that is the new element against which we object. Because it is sufficient to say, we can say from 2 metres high, we can see everything, for instance. And the confrontation of these two images show us very well, what is the danger of wanting to apply computerisation at any price in this trial, in this case. And this is our main objection. We cannot accept that the computerisation is trying people, even if it is in the 21st century. Mr. President, the second part which I wish to enlarge upon, is that this map is more visible in its longitude and its latitude. That means that we can also work with the diagonal. But what I do know is that it was perfectly capable to obtain such a map much before the testimony of the witnesses and we know that a system was applied as from 1996 and 1997. And what I do not understand is why they did not wish to have -- to produce such a map so that the witnesses can have a look at it, rather than having them lose their bearings. And in spite of the position of the Defence from the very start we said we will not be able to work this map, and we were told a lot of things about equator and such like. And finally we have got a map which is a little more visible, but this should have been done beforehand rather than now, producing maps on which witnesses will not be able to give information because they didn't have the necessary information. Thank you. Because they didn't want to be given -- they didn't want to give them the right information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's an allegation which -- may I first ask the -- Mr. Ierace, the map as it is shown to us now, that means without stretching on either the longitudinal or the other direction, could that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. technically be done before? Could that -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the -- in terms of the software that the OTP has, it could not practically have been done until the 6th of November. I am told that we received an intermediate update of the software approximately nine months ago, but for various technical reasons, we didn't have the ability to properly produce a map with the corrected projections, if you like, to enable a measurement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, then do I understand that when Mr. Piletta-Zanin asks you why you did not produce it, but why you did not wish to produce it, the leading element in that question, that is the assumption that you did not wish to do it, that you reject it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I absolutely reject that. Before the Prosecution case began, we did everything we could to come up with maps that were legible in the sense of with contours that could easily be seen with distances that could easily be measured. And that was the best we could do at that stage. As soon as I learned of this software which happily coincided with the expression of the Trial Chamber of some concerns about the ability to measure distances, I took steps to see what could be done with it produce maps such as what we now have. This is effectively hot off the press. Mr. President, in relation to the discrepancy that Mr. Piletta-Zanin points out between the sample I gave him yesterday and the draft today, that is explicable by where one places the suspected source of fire with absolute precision. The one yesterday had that source of fire placed roughly in the centre of the circle or oval now, and this shows the view from the edge. I would like to see these maps with the circle shaded area, now an oval shaded area, transparent so that one can see the contours and the terrain beneath it. And it demonstrates the sensitivity of the software to changes in the topography depending on where the person is, and what distance they are above the ground. And I am happy to provide the Trial Chamber with the relevant information which led to the map yesterday, as well as the map -- the information which leads to the lines of sight in this map. Might I just emphasise, Mr. President: At this stage it seems to me the important features are the ability to measure distances between two points and the more visible contour lines. As to lines of sight, what can be seen and can't be seen, Prosecution laid evidence in its case by way of photographs and eyewitness evidence as to lines of sight. The Defence has raised some further issues for the first time, such as the height of trees and orchards, and the Prosecution reserves its right to respond to issues raised for the first time in case in rebuttal, and that includes lines of sight. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very briefly. I have the impression --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I have the impression that the Prosecution didn't really respond to the Defence in a sense that the question asked was to find out, and this is what the Defence would like to know, to know whether this software is extremely sensitive, whether this software existed at the time when the problems already appeared with these maps, at the time of the Prosecution case, that is, there are many months from that now. And the Defence believes that such software existed at the time of that case, and I think we've had the confirmation of that by the Prosecution. At the time when the problems appeared, they should have been resolved and not at the time of the Defence case. And we maintain that in a way our rights have been offended because it is very hard to work with the witnesses on these maps when they don't recognise the locations any more or areas that have been distorted in reality on the layout of the map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Is it the position of the Defence that you should always provide the most updated material you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. The position of the Defence is that one shouldn't always produce documents that are erroneous, and what we are saying is that these maps are erroneous and we can see now, and we are reiterating, it is not about using high technology, it is about having things presented in a clear way. And to have given just an ordinary map would have been a lot simpler and would have been a lot less costly for the international community, and really I think this should be a very large effort, a considerable effort being made here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, your argument is clear. We will hear further details from Mr. Ierace later today. Madam Usher, can you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. DP16, because we will call you DP16, since protective measures have been granted in respect to you. That means we will not say your name and your face cannot be seen apart from in this courtroom by ourselves.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. Good morning to you, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP16, before giving testimony in this court, the Rules of Procedure and Evidence require you to make a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. The text of this solemn declaration will be handed out to you now by the usher. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean aloud?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Aloud, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please be seated, Mr. DP16. You will first be examined by counsel for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, good morning.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: First of all, with the assistance of the usher, I am going to hand you a piece of paper and if you could please have a look at it, read it and if the information contained on this sheet of paper is correct, just confirm that that is the case, just say yes, if that's not the case, then say no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, they're correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the sense that we would like to ask some questions of situations and personal details --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since we are in open session, you may proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, please bear in mind what I told you earlier. If you may give any information, stop and ask if we can go to another form of session. Thank you. Witness, where were you exactly in the spring of 1992, what memory do you have of that period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Spring 1992. You probably mean the very beginning of armed conflict or just before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, very much so. I am talking about the period that was just before the breakout of the conflict, and then of course that period itself.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: When we are talking about this problem, then we should start with the month of March 1992, that is from the period of the first barricades in the city of Sarajevo. I was, throughout that period, in Sarajevo, but most of the time, of course, together with my family near the place where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened to you from the moment when things started to get worse following the barricades that you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The barricades lasted, I think, two days and two nights, that is, the beginning of March. And I believe that the purpose of the barricades was to make the leadership of Bosnia-Herzegovina more serious so that they shouldn't make any mistakes. There was a kind of self-organisation that happened of certain groups of people and nations in the city of Sarajevo. That's what it looked like in reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you spoke about self-organisation, can you tell us more about this self-organisation? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: That really demands for an explanation and not really to state the fact itself. To state the fact itself, that is to say that we, and I now represent just part of the Serbs, only part of the Serbs who lived in the territory where I lived, and part of the Muslims who lived in our immediate vicinity. We were --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that. I ask that that be redacted. The witness doesn't speak for part of the Serbs or part of the Muslims, but for himself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand your answer to be that you did not feel -- that you did not have the same feelings and thoughts as you consider all the Serbs would have. Is that how I have to understand your answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the witness can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Please, Witness, proceed with what you were going to say.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: On the ground things happened as follows: We, the Serbs, and Muslims who were in our immediate vicinity in the location where I lived in a self-organised manner had put up these barricades. And at some part of these barricades we had a joint guard, that is, the joint barricade, which was supposed to represent security for both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Could you just give us some information, not about the barricades themselves, but on the way that the idea appeared to put up, to erect, these protective measures? Initially, how did that -- where did this idea come from to proceed to this self-protection?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Well, you see, we were all neighbours after all, and this very term "neighbour" is very strong in Bosnia-Herzegovina and has meaning. And this protection that I mentioned earlier, that is the joint barricade, was evidence itself for ordinary people, that is, for women and children, for the elderly, and for the people who were not willing to participate in any kind of intense clashes. And that was proof about the possibility of resolving a problem differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But that is the fact of the barricade. But the decision-making process itself, and perhaps I am addressing you as philosopher, how did that happen? How did this idea -- how was this idea born in the spirit of the people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: You mean self-organisation or the barricades themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I mean the self-organisation.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In Bosnia-Herzegovina, all of us and particularly in Sarajevo, Sarajevo was a political for of Bosnia-Herzegovina, we were all more or less forced to follow political events in the immediate vicinity, and also wider and further afield in the -- throughout the former Yugoslavia. We were aware, we were conscious that something bad was going to happen. And this organisation was the result of the bad politics of some politicians that I wouldn't name individually. But in relation to the organisation of that part of the State of Bosnia-Herzegovina, at that time the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, that part composed of Serbs. I would put this different, from a historical point of view, I can state the fact that all the peoples who lived in that part of the Balkans, in my opinion, in some way have the pressure of history from the bad side, which is, in my opinion again, one of the key reasons why the self-organisation happened on the level of defence from the neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You spoke about -- you spoke about self-organisation, to start with, and then you spoke about self-protection. Now, I would like to suggest that after the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because Mr. President, it seems to me that it is time for the break --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: That you tell us about the second part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that it is now time to have a break. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace, I think we should first continue with the witness, perhaps, for a while because so many interruptions is not good for a witness. And I think it is not of vital importance that we hear your information on the maps right now, but we could hear it at a later stage today. Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke to us about self-organisation before the break, on the one hand, and at the same time you spoke about self-defence. So my question is self-defence against whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: If there is self-organisation by a group of people, then it was done precisely for the purpose of self-defence against another group of people which, in this case, conditionally speaking were Muslims. But why am I saying "conditionally"? Because at that point in time there was the Territorial Defence consisting only of one group of people in Sarajevo. We are aware of the fact that the absolute majority were Muslims, and I am also aware and I can testify under oath in my personal name that within our group the majority were Serbs, but they were not all Serbs. And that is what the self-defence was like. There were certain parts of the city of Sarajevo in which certain people dominated as being the majority population in that area. And that is how those self-defence groups were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, you mentioned this distinction between Serbs on the one hand and the Muslims on the other. During the period you are describing, that is, the period immediately preceding the beginning of the armed conflict, what did you see in the streets that would be of interest to this Chamber? I am referring specifically regarding the activities and organisation of the part called the Muslim part or the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: What is of interest and what was conspicuous to all the citizens of Sarajevo was the emergence of the so-called Green Berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me stop you there. In two words, will you tell us what the Green Berets were, and above all, when they appeared, as far as you can recollect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: A Green Beret is a green military cap worn by a certain group of people, and later on it became a military formation called the Green Berets, and as far as I can remember, they appeared in the streets of Sarajevo at the end of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When they appeared in the streets of all Sarajevo, were they organised in groups or did they appear individually?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Usually in town I would see them individually in the streets, in the trams, trolley buses, buses, but as an organisation I noticed them when I went to Television Sarajevo to appear as a guest in one of their programmes. They examined my ID documents and they engaged in the security affairs which until then was done by the regular police that we would see every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us when this happened, this particular event that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: This event occurred in March 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When exactly, at the beginning, in the middle?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: At the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And where exactly did this occur? You said that you went to the television building. Was it on the premises, on the way there, at the entrance, could you be more precise, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Like all Security Services they were at the entrance to the Sarajevo television building.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have the feeling that these people were a part of the institution, the television itself; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How would these people tolerated by such an institution because after all, the people in the institution knew them, if you know, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to leading and the question in any event is inappropriately addressed to this witness because it seeks a comment as to the attitude of the institution.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. If I may respond. He did not comment on the attitude of the institution -- I didn't comment on it. I just asked the witness whether --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... different way. Do you know anything about the television institute, whether they agreed with the presence of these people next to the building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I can give you a negative answer, but I would like to add a sentence, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so you say you do not know anything about it, but you would like to add a sentence. Please add that sentence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that they looked the same as any security service in certain institutions. Up to then it would be the police wearing regular police uniforms which we had come to be accustomed to. This time they were wearing different uniforms, green military uniforms, not the uniforms of the police. And the others were not present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did you notice that the security was provided by different people from what you experienced before, but you do not have any knowledge as to whether the television institute would have agreed with their presence or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree with what you have just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you spoke about green uniforms. Was there anything else in addition to those uniforms that this group called the Green Berets were wearing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In the streets I didn't see them carrying any weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: In the streets. In any other places apart from the streets, did you see anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Only in this particular place that I went to visit, that is the television building, they did have pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You were saying that you went there yourself. Did you go there on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, I went on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, I should now like you to tell us how -- no, I withdraw that. Could you please tell us what you personally did at the time the armed conflict in Sarajevo started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I had a private company which --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, no. I will stop you there. I don't wish you to give us such identifying information, and on the other hand, that was not my question. At the moment the time the war broke out in Sarajevo did you take part in it, that is my first question; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: If you are talking about the war that went on from 1992 to 1995, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Where were you stationed and during which period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Throughout the time of the war I was at Grbavica, that is where I was stationed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you tell us with greater precision what part of the line did you defend in those days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: My group of men was positioned at the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You will certainly be asked to draw those positions, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. but since you are talking about the Jewish cemetery, I have several questions for you. Do you know whether there was any construction at the bottom of the Jewish cemetery? Was there a building there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us what type of building it was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: There was a chapel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And this chapel, was it within the cemetery walls; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, Witness, whether this chapel, as you call it, was - and if so during which period - in the hands of one of the conflicting parties in this area; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us which side held control of this chapel and for what period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: For the duration of the war it was held by the Muslim party.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How do you know this? How are you able to assert that in this Chamber?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I looked at it with my own eyes throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you see during the duration of the war soldiers of the BH Army entering, leaving the building or occupying that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Whatever you have mentioned, I would see during the war and something else that you did not mention, and that is that they opened fire from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say that they opened fire from it, was this occasional or something that happened frequently or very frequently? What could you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Certainly it was very frequent.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And what type of weapons were used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What was the direction or directions in which fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Towards the positions -- the positions of the group of people I belonged to were west of the Jewish cemetery, so the direction was towards the west.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Did you return fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: As frequently as they opened it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And as you were a soldier during the time of the war, did you ever receive instructions, Witness, from the military structures regarding: One, the opening of fire; and two, the problem or the question of respecting the rights of the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: We received orders from the high command through our commander, that is, our immediate superiors in relation to us ordinary soldiers. And all these orders boiled down to economising with the ammunition and absolute respect of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. To make things even more clear, could you tell us in general terms what was your military training?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I personally did not serve, do my military service in the Yugoslav People's Army, so that I have no military experience. I had no military experience prior to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, you mentioned the instructions you received. I would like you to tell us the frequency with which those instructions were conveyed to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In any case, every time when we had to go and fetch fresh ammunition, and sometimes with greater frequency.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But I am also talking about the protection of the civilian population when opening fire.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Could you be clearer, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am -- I had asked you about economy with the ammunition and you answered that question. The second aspect had to do with instructions given you regarding the necessary attention that should be paid to the civilian population, in other words, the protection of civilians during combat. What was the incidence with which such instructions were given to you? I am no longer talking about ammunition, but about the protection of the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Those types of instructions were very frequent, but I must observe that the civilian population could not be seen by us in the immediate vicinity of the separation lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Could you tell us what your company was and your unit were, your companies and units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In the first stage of the war, it was a 3rd company of the 3rd Battalion, and in the last stages of the war, my company changed and in the same battalion I was a member of the Novo Sarajevo Chetnik detachment which was a separate detachment, a separate company of that same detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. But still in the same position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I, personally, was not in the same position, but the zone of responsibility was the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, before we ask you to point to the front lines on a map that will be shown to you, will you please answer this question: I am not speaking strictly about the front line, but rather of the depth of the line, that is, the technical depth, that is various services, the supplies, and the command areas. According to your experience, what were the depths of the front lines in the broader sense of the word?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: This is a question that it will be difficult to answer correctly, but if I am talking about Grbavica as a part of the territory of the city of Sarajevo which during the war was held by the Serbs, there was no depth virtually, though large -- an enormous number of the civilian inhabitants, and I am referring to women, children and the elderly, stayed on to live in that area. But one could conditionally speak of the depth between the front lines of roughly one -- behind the front lines of roughly 100 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, where was the headquarters of the battalion, what was the distance between it and the closest front line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The command of my battalion was roughly 1 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And also, could you tell us what was the distance between the closest front line and the command of the company this time, your company command headquarters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Then the distance would be only a few dozen metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I will now show you a map with the assistance of the usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I should like to point out that we didn't have a sufficiently long piece of paper to copy everything that we wanted to copy, and that is why some maps could not be copied.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the map being shown to you and placed on the ELMO; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, will you please take note of two things that are noted: First of all, not to write anything on the map unless you are asked to do so; and secondly, when the Defence asks you to write things, to do so with a black pen and never with a blue one. Witness, could you find on this map the places where you were stationed as a soldier during the events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness is pointing to an area situated slightly to the right of the word "Grbavica" that we can see on the map, south of the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question now has to do with the other riverbank. On the other side of the river, were there cultural monuments or religious monuments of importance, such as, for instance, mosques; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I didn't hear your answer, Witness, I am sorry. Could the microphone be placed closer to you, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just for the transcript, where the witness pointed and where you said it was right of the word "Grbavica," I would say that it was approximately in the area where the -- between the streets indicated by Luka Teli and Travnicka on the map close to an area where some symbols as to -- at least close to a small green area. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you answered "yes" but could you please repeat your answer, whether religious monuments, cultural or religious monuments were on the other side facing you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: You said across the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, could you please pick up a pen and indicate, for instance, if there were any, could you tell us where were the museums that were right facing your positions, and since I was also speaking about religious facilities, the mosques. First of all, museums.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: From this position where I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Just simply opposite Grbavica, what were the museums? I think that it is possible to distinguish them, to find them on this map. Could you please just put a circle around that point.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Here was the national museum.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You circled two facilities. Is that the same -- the same facility in reality? We see two "M's on the map, is there one museum or is there two museums?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: These are two museum, one is national, and one is the revolution museum which is the museum which was made as to memory -- in memory of the Second World War.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please just put a number 1 and a number 2 there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you please point to a mark which is opposite of Grbavica also on the same area visible on this map.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: First of all, what's visible is the Catholic church.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Can you please mark the Catholic church also. Could you put number "3" there. And then I'd ask you to mark a mosque which is in this area, if there were any.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, there was -- perhaps I am going to make a mistake, because it is not visible from the positions, but its location was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I know that you don't have military experience or not very long military experience, but do you know if one or more of these objects or these facilities could be hit by indirect hits, that is, by mortar fire? This is a hypothetical question. I am not saying that you targeted these facilities, but it is -- was it possible to hit these facilities with mortars, with mortar fire; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The transcript does not reflect that the witness circled the mosque. Perhaps the circle could be marked with a number so that it can be correlated to the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggest we take number "4."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise and I thank the Prosecution for pointing it out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please put a "4" to where you circled the mosque.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did mark number "4."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but -- yes, please proceed, then. That does not appear in the transcript, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I withdraw my thanks to the Prosecution, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, that was just uncourtesy. You would have understood, yes. Yes, I take note.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question is the following, you answered yes, it was possible theoretically and technically speaking, it was possible to hit with indirect fire these facilities. And in relation to number 4, and it is also valid for the 3, the 2 and the 1, also, did you ever receive any instructions, any orders from your military hierarchy, from your superiors, to target in any way possible one of the four of these facilities; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever received instructions, orders, from your military superiors that would have made you target similar facilities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Witness, could you please now take time and draw, if you can, the confrontation line as you have known it, but first of all, could you please point to it with a pointer so that we can avoid a possibility of an error. Take -- could you please pick up the pointer and point to where you think the line went and then you can mark it with a black pen. And perhaps just to make this task simpler, Witness, Witness, Witness? Witness? Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
