utterances.text: I am sorry. Could you also please give the names of the streets so that we can later on find them in the transcript. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I will start with the Serbian part which goes from this hill called Zlatiste, and the line went below this yellow road. And here there is a hill called Staro Brdo, and then the line went this way, turned this way, and here this empty space is the so-called Debelo Brdo, and the line then went down to the top of Travnicka Street and it followed the 315, that's number 315, and then it followed the wall of the Jewish cemetery. This street called, now called wrongly because these are the postwar street names, probably before the war the street was called Nevesinjska Street and this street went to the bottom of the Jewish cemetery and then up to number 397, which is the continuation of the Travnicka Street and then following the yellow road, so-called transit road at the time of the war it was empty, deserted, there were no trenches there but the trench went below the road. The ground is sloping downwards here towards the Miljacka river and then the line went along Ljubljanska Street that you can see here, and then it followed the line 409 which is Trnovska Street, that's its old street and then down there there was a Beogradska Street where there was a famous red building, and at number, somewhere near 533 that we can see on the map, that's where the building was where the bank, the economy bank of Sarajevo was located, and that was the last trench on the Miljacka river.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please now pick up a pen and can you just go back and follow this itinerary on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I should like Madam Usher if she could zoom it on this route, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. In relation to this line that you drew, I would be grateful if you could now place a cross and a number "5" at the point that you previously called the chapel, please. The chapel.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And since we are speaking about the enemy lines, could you please draw but with a dotted line, not with a full line, the positions of the opposing side, of the enemy side in this area, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I can see that you have established the first pocket. But does it mean that there was a problem, a mistake, with this pocket or was there some kind of a network of the trenches and sort of intersection? Did you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, precisely here. Yes, you are probably speaking about this part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: For the moment I just forgot that above the Jewish cemetery, that's the famous Debelo Brdo, where the Muslim units had created a pocket with the system of trenches -- with the communication trenches, and here, below here, it says Staro Brdo, but in fact it was Zlatiste, there was also a pocket here where they had very strong sniper strongholds.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. You spoke to us about a hill which is called Debelo Brdo. Now, as this name suggests, this was a point that was higher than your positions, I am speaking about Debelo Brdo.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. You spoke about that the opposing side had weapons on that hill. What kind of weapons did the opposing side have on that hill?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In any case, these were infantry weapons with the reservation that in that pocket that is at the very end of it, end point, there was a very strong sniper nest, what kind of weapon it is exactly, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, on this hill was there anything else that was located there, apart from the infantry weapons? Was there anything else on Debelo Brdo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: On Debelo Brdo, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Were there positions with heavy weapons, with types of heavy weapons in that area, and I am talking about the enemy positions on the enemy side.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do object to leading on any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will rephrase.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness -- no, I will rephrase. You said that you -- there was firing on you from the direction of the famous chapel. Do you remember you said that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Was this the only place from which you were fired at; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So there were other locations?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us with which weapons were you targeted; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: From all kinds of weapons that is used in war, fire was opened on my lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Specifically speaking, there, this location during that period, what type of weapons are you speaking about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: All types of shells that were at the disposal of the -- disposal of the Army of the then Yugoslavia, they were at the disposal of the BH Army and those shells were falling on our lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. You are speaking about the shells. But as far as direct targeting is concerned, not indirect targeting, what kind of weapons were used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In any case, all calibres from 556 to 12.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Starting from which calibre do we consider a weapon "heavy weapon" do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: As far as I know, from 12.7.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What was the heavy weapon used, because you said 12.7?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Its abbreviation, it's Pat, that is anti-aircraft gun or cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since you came under fire, that kind of fire, I conclude that this fire was fired open from these Pat guns, and this was used in horizontal mode or as we call it, the ground mode.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do object to leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are giving all details you expect from the answer. That's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So would you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Mr. President. Indeed, but I was trying to save time, considering that the witness said that he was fired at, and he was fired at with an anti-aircraft gun, and if he was not up in the air, then it is very likely that he was fired at in ground mode. So that is what I was trying to find out. So I have to find out differently now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, how do you explain that you were fired at with an anti-aircraft gun, although you were not up in the air? Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: This war that went on in Bosnia-Herzegovina is probably one of the very characteristic wars, the way that it was fought, and that's the only way that I can interpret this, except that I would just like to make a slight correction as to the abbreviation that I said for 12.7. It is not a Pat, but it is a Pam, that is an anti-aircraft machine gun, although Pat was also used in -- for ground combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. How was this Pam, the anti-aircraft gun, used considering that you were not in the air, but you were on the ground, do you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: And did I know because on several occasions I was targeted by this very same Pam, and I can draw and show you this location where the Pam fired from and where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. DP16, have you any knowledge on the modes that can be used in anti-aircraft guns? Do you have any knowledge about how to use such a weapon, the ways it can be used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, personal experience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do you know what modes can be used?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would be the different ways of using such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of the modes, specifically speaking, is that I was personally targeted with an anti-aircraft machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you use such a weapon, how would you use that, to do what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in a position to be near that machine-gun, but I never used it. So I can't answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, tell me how can you be certain that this machine-gun was used, very briefly, when you were targeted by it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: If I had known that you would ask me that, then I would have brought the bullet or rather several bullets that were targeting me, that's the only way that I had proved it to myself what I was targeted with by some people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You wanted to identify the location from which you were targeted. Could you please indicate it on the map; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Could you please point to it and could you now please -- I believe now we are at number "6," mark number "6".

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness has done so. Would you please indicate the direction of fire, covering this machine-gun, this anti-aircraft machine-gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: From this position towards the locality of Grbavica. So that would be a wide area, wider area towards Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness points to the back of his lines to the west of the map in the direction of the word "Grbavica."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would be grateful if we could have a more specific description, either perhaps you should do it, Mr. President, or I am happy to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please point again exactly where they fired it from, from there to -- in what direction?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this here. From location number "6" in the westerly direction in the direction of Grbavica towards Vraca, up to the centre, urban centre of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness pointed from point "6" in westerly direction, from south a little below where it reads "Vraca" on the map, up north to Grbavica, the built-up area, even a little bit further north from the word "Grbavica" itself. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you see other weapons that were active and used by the opposing army, specifically, artillery weapons that were used?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: As far as the city of Sarajevo is concerned from which fire was opened towards Grbavica and our positions, I personally saw two combat vehicles, both were tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Where did you see them, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: One tank I saw on the Hum hill which faces the south, that is, faces us, and it is on the northern side of Sarajevo. And the second tank I saw going out of the tunnel at the Ciglana locality.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: We have heard much evidence from this witness about specific incidents, nothing as to time frame of what the Defence calls "chronology." The witness has said that he was there throughout the war, as I understand it. It is of little use without a time frame. And my respectful submission is that should be done in chief, and not in cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, especially if you are not talking about positions that might have been held for a longer period of time, but such observations as to tanks, would you please ask the witness to specify a time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I will specify, yes. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to these two tanks, first question, before the time frame question, was this tank active; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. When, if you can say this, when did you see it or when did you know that these tanks were active, which period, which year, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: According to what people -- what I heard from people throughout the war, but from what I have seen, that was at the end of 1992 and the beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And it was firing in which direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In the direction that I can indicate, which is the direction of Debelo Brdo, that is, the barracks Bosut.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: And Zlatiste, these lines held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness indicates the barracks located practically on the line where there is a large pocket that is marked on the map, and then in an area which is bluish, slightly below, above the word "Staro Brdo."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, the same question for the time frame or chronology in relation to the Pam, what you called anti-aircraft machine-gun --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it could create some confusion where you said it was -- he was pointing at an area north, at least above Staro Brdo. He pointed at an area just south of the line he has drawn as being the VRS line, just on a relatively empty area north-west of where it reads "Staro Brdo." Where he indicated before where was Debelo Brdo. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just another matter. The witness has told us he has saw two tanks, one on Hum, one at the Ciglana tunnel. It is not at all clear which of the two tanks he is referring to as having fired at the barracks. Perhaps that could be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, that can be done through the cross-examination. The witness said that he saw both tanks opening fire, so he used the plural.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you, Mr. DP16, how often did you see the tank at the tunnel firing in late 1992, early 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, very rarely, but it did open fire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but how often? One time? Five times? 10 times? 25 times? Approximately. I am not asking a --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judging by what I personally saw, it was five times. I personally saw that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I was looking for. And the same question for the tank at Hum hill. How often did you personally see that tank fire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That tank, according to what I saw, opened fire only once towards Grbavica, because it was deployed on a BH Army positions facing the northern part of the separation line between the Army of Republika Srpska and their forces in the area of Vogosca, so that it opened fire in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you saw it firing only once to Grbavica. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, what was the distance between Hum and your position as the crow flies, approximately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Hum and the position of the Jewish cemetery in my judgment, the distance is more than 3 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And the shell reached the area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: It wasn't the tank from Hum, but from Ciglana.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I see. Thank you. The same question for the anti-aircraft machine-gun. From when was it used, et cetera, during which time period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Very soon after the beginning of the war and throughout the duration of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Regarding weapons generally, Witness, you told us that you were self-organised. What did you know about the organisation of the adversary regarding the question of armaments, specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: As far as the organisation of defence in Sarajevo is concerned, I think that it was very similar to the way our side was organised. As for weapons, in the city of Sarajevo we all know that a number of buildings that used to be used by the Yugoslav People's Army which when they left Sarajevo or rather when the JNA withdrew from the territory of Sarajevo and beyond, a large portion of the weapons was left behind in the barracks, so that it was accessible to the opposing side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you please give us brief answers, as far as you can. To be specific, do you know whether the adversary had access to those weapons in the barracks; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: This was shown on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, did you know of any industrial facilities that were situated opposite your positions in Grbavica; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Specifically, facing my line there were no industrial facilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Are you aware of a building that could have been used for industrial purposes by the adversary; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do object to leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I be heard, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that the question is leading. I am just asking the witness whether he knew certain things, and I am saying -- using the term, a building that could have been used. I don't see how else we could proceed. I don't see how else -- in what other way I could put that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- as a matter of principle, I think every building could be used for, that's rather my problem than leading, perhaps. Whether it seeks speculation, let me just read the answers -- the questions again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- To save time, perhaps I can rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: We've spoken about weapons, Witness. This was at the beginning of the war. Do you know how the problem of weapons as well as that of ammunition was addressed and resolved, perhaps, by the so-called Muslim forces in Sarajevo as the hostilities developed? What do you know about that, if you know anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I can say something about that thanks to my experience as to what was used to open fire at us and what fell upon us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, please do that, briefly.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In the first stage of the war, it is true that the Muslim forces had poor or poorer weapons and they used home-made shells and explosives, mines and explosives. And what fell on us was an indication of this. In any event, one could call that amateurish.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. And as from when did the situation change, according to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Upon the withdrawal of the Yugoslav People's Army, following their withdrawal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you give us the exact date, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: It may be difficult, but in any event it was in May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Will you please concentrate on the map to your right and I would like you to add some information on that map. Was there, Witness, in this area in which the two parties were in confrontation, were there any military observation posts? And I am, of course, referring to UN positions.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, there were.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you localise them and use the following numbers: 7, et cetera, onwards, from 7 on.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In the immediately vicinity of the bridge, the Vrbanja Bridge, there was a French unit post behind the chapel, behind number "5." On this yellow road was an observation post number "8" held by French units. At the top of Debelo Brdo, there was another French observation post, number "9," and at the top of the Jewish cemetery number "10" was a position held by Russian forces. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Again I object on the grounds of relevance, unless we have the chronology, unless we have the times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Gladly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you please tell us when those observation posts were established, please, and for how long they remained there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I may be mistaken regarding the month, but January, February or March 1994, and until the end of the war they remained there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, would you please now tell us with respect to a map --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we were not able to copy everything, but before that, as I have -- before showing another map, we would like to submit another exhibit which will be D334, with the assistance of the usher, whom we thank. The coloured ones for the Chamber and a coloured one for the witness. I have another coloured copy. There were three for the Chamber, but something happened which I don't criticise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this building that we see on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is a red building. Is it the red building you mentioned a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us where it was situated on the map indicating the name of the street, could you point to it on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If the map has gone, we will ask it to be brought back. How can you explain what -- that something seems to be missing in the middle of this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: May I -- shall I mark with a number this location?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Number "11."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, perhaps we could put the photograph on the screen again. Could you leave the map there, please, as well. Put the photograph on top, please, photograph on top.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, there is an empty space in this building. Do you know how it occurred, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The Muslim and Serb units were separated in that building by a single wall of one apartment. Because of continuous and direct provocations and firing, what happened was that a part of this building toppled because inside there were gas installations, because before the war, this building had heating by gas.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there destruction of this kind in Grbavica, I mean, within the area that you were defending, that is Grbavica, and if so what were the causes of such destruction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The answer is yes, but as a rule the only major damage was on the very front lines of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can remove the photograph and show the witness a map. Unfortunately, Mr. President, we didn't find any maps that were not previously marked, but we will tell the witness not to pay any attention to the indications on this map, if that is acceptable to everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that the question you put to the witness are unrelated to the markings already appearing on the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they are unrelated, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, may I ask you one clarification. When you asked the building in the photograph was the red building he mentioned before, and since I tried to understand the context, I couldn't find where the witness referred to a red building before, so I am missing the context.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said very quickly, I don't know whether he said it in Serbian, because I can't follow all three languages at the same time. I know he mentioned it. As far as I can recollect, he mentioned when he was taking up the pointer and before drawing the line, I see him nodding his head, so my memory is good, he was indicating where the line was going. And when he ended his description, he said this is where a red building was, but I can look it up, if necessary. It was at that point in time when he mentioned it.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Page 50, line 17.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I missed it. I apologise for the time taken. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness to your right is a map, do you recognise that area?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't have a copy of that map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have two got copies and my equality is not always fully respected.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I hope that everyone has a map now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this area appearing on your -- to your right and on your screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, only it is more magnified than it was a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps, Madam Usher, we could send her on the area around 24 and the red circle that we see on the map, that we could focus in on that. Thank you very much. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would be grateful if you could disregard the two blue lines that you see on this map. And I would also be grateful if with a black marker you could localise, if you can, the place where the defence lines of the adversary were. Use a black pen and do so in a dotted line. If they are the same, you can just leave them. I am talking about the lines held by the adversary.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Have you indicated thereby, the lines held by the adversary, that is the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness could you indicate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, just for clarification for myself, was this line held by the adversary during the whole conflict? Did it ever change or was it stable during the whole conflict, Mr. DP16?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the exception of these two pockets, the rest of the line was stable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It didn't change.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say the two pockets, you mean the pockets on the south of the cemetery, the first one, and the second one, Debelo Brdo. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again it would be helpful to the Prosecution in terms of the indictment period to know whether the pockets were existent during the indictment period or after or before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say that the pockets, that's where the lines changed. Were the pockets made later and then when?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These pockets were made on the 6th of January 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Both of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's very clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You went around the red circle on this map. Could you, as we are not on the same map as before, what was situated inside that red circle, within the red circle, if there was anything in it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The chapel at the Jewish cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would be grateful if you could place a "K", a single "K" within that circle, if you could, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And for things to be quite clear, you spoke to us a moment ago of a chapel held and occupied by the adversary, that is the Muslim forces. Is that the same buildings that you have just marked with a "K"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, at any point in time during the conflict did the forces of the VRS or the Serb forces use this chapel during the conflict; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, the indication of the cemetery is given a name, the word is written out, and also it is lighter in colour; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. What were -- what was on the edges of the cemetery? Was there something that marked the area in reality, physically, that 1s the area of the cemetery?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, there was a large stone wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "a large stone wall, you mean large in terms of length, or breadth or height or all three? Or you mean something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: All of that together.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Roughly how high was the wall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Two to three metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I must then ask you how then could you see people entering and leaving the chapel, you yourself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The place that I will indicate now to you is a small hill with an orchard from which I had a view over the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Will you please not mark anything on the map, unless you are asked to do so. Thank you. I would now like to ask you something else. Do you know what a Dragonov is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, for the transcript, the witness marked a very small circle approximately in the middle, just west of the cemetery on the map. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know what a Dragonov is; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, from your positions, whatever they were, did you have a line of sight, a direct line of sight to the point that one could see before, but we can't see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we must enlarge the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So from your positions, wherever you were, did you have a direct line of sight towards point "24" and how?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: First of all, because I lived in the area all my life. I know all positions exactly by heart. And this map does not reflect the real state of affairs on the ground. So that point "24" is not visible from the position I was in because the view was obstructed by some buildings that are in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you show those buildings to us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: This building is the Assembly building of Bosnia-Herzegovina which obstructs the view to the crossroads at Marijn Dvor and plus, this area here is also walled in with a large wall, and these buildings are actually an old warehouse that burned down in the first days of the war. And those walls also obstructed the view to this position, and specifically, the crossroads on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the witness pointed to two buildings. The first, the first image is to the north of the word "Marijn Dvor" or more precisely, the word "V-O-R" and in a lighter colour right next to it, several buildings in a schematic form, forming a polygon of red colour that are the warehouses the witness was mentioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The last question before the break, you spoke about the perimeter wall and I was asking you about the view that you might have had of the red dot marked with a number "24." Let me ask you the same question now, but in a hypothetical sense, not regarding the line of sight, but a line of fire. Was it possible, as far as you know, to be able to fire at and hit point "24" from the positions that you held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Do you mean infantry weapons such as a rifle?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am talking about a direct -- direct fire, yes, rifles.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: From positions that I was at, it is impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't know whether the break is now or at a quarter to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The break is now, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Yes. We will adjourn until 10 minutes to 1.00. May I ask you, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, how much time you would approximately need? I know that you are not yet at the time indicated, but, of course, the experience of the last few days gave hope to the Chamber that all parties would speed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are referring to the days when I was absent, I am sure, Mr. President. It will be relatively brief, as it has been the past few days, but I am not able to tell you just now. I have to confer with my lead counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To now, I think you used 1 hour and 40 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, as for the other topic, do you wish that be discussed today or should I go straight into cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It also matters how we proceed with this witness and I will perhaps take a decision whether we will deal with it today or later. I know I am always stealing minutes from you. We will adjourn until 5 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, welcome again into the courtroom. And with the assistance of Madam Usher and of course with the leave of Mr. President, we will ask you to have a look at some photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the Exhibit number is D339. D339. And I'd ask Madam Usher to put the photograph on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this view that you can see on the screen; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. In the centre, in the middle more or less of the image, and there is a yellow building, and perhaps we could zoom on the two buildings in the centre of the photograph that we are interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please zoom a little more, please. A little more. Thank you. Stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: These are two -- oh, yes, here it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please zoom again because we had lost -- thank you. Stop here. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise the picture or rather the building which is to the left, the building which has a yellow facade, can you see that, yellow walls, outside walls; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Holiday Inn Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, do you know if this building was used for other purposes, apart from civilian purposes, during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You don't know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Not from personal experience, but according to information.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: From what sources?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: From the people who came from the parts of Sarajevo under the control of Muslim forces and they were crossing over to our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. For the French booth, it is not the "other towns" but the other parts of the town. And what did they tell you? What did you learn from them?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, Mr. President, on the same basis as on earlier occasions, we now -- the witness is now invited to tell us what he has been told by unknown persons at unknown times in relation to uses at unknown times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, Mr. President, this is rather surprising from someone who has issued an indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is rejected. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the Chamber understands that it is sometimes difficult to have direct sources available from information, what happened at the other side of confrontation lines. On the other hand, you also should be aware that since the other party, the Prosecution in this case, is not able to cross-examine the sources, that, of course, the probative value will have to be assessed at a later stage. And the more precise you are in relation to the sources, the lesser the disadvantage for the Prosecution will be. So please keep that in mind, but we will allow such questions on hearsay, but I thought it wise to make the observations I just did. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. First of all, I apologise. I didn't see that you were conferring, and I thought I had your invitation to respond.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, could you specify with giving us small details with regard to the information that you had about this building, with more details?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, precisely that. The fact is that a large number of people of Serb nationality crossed over to this side from the Muslim part, that is from the part of the city of Sarajevo that was held by the Muslim units. And the sources are these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. To the extent that these people told you about this, for what purposes was this building used for?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question presumes that the communication was direct to this witness. He has not yet said that. Perhaps we could clarify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we first try to find out better about the sources, because that is a problem, of course, if we allow hearsay. Please clarify this issue first, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Among these people who left the city and would have brought information with them, were there some of them that you knew directly and who had spoken directly to you about this; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you, yes or no, give their names?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: That shouldn't be a problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, should I proceed with the names in which case we perhaps would have to go into closed session or can we be satisfied with this demonstration?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we should be as detailed as possible in this respect. We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, without giving the names of the people that you have told us about, can you tell us, what did these people tell you directly to you about this building and about its use for military purposes?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes. They told us the moment when they crossed over, that is in the discussions we had after they crossed over, that this building apart from it being used publicly as the seat of the journalists from the entire world, this part of the building that was facing us, that's facing us on the photograph, that this part of the building was used for military purposes, that it had its positions from which firing -- fire was open towards the positions of the Republika Srpska Army at Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say "from where firing was open" what with was fire opened, from which weapons, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Infantry weapons, ordinary rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Are you here referring to a specific type of military action?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: In any case, your question demands a larger explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you are able to do that, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The way of waging war in Sarajevo was specific, particularly in this territory, in the urban area of the city of Sarajevo, all taller buildings were used as sniper positions and as such, particularly they were used during more intense conflicts or during attacks on the positions of the Republika Srpska Army, as support for the depth for the units that were trying to break through the lines of defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are saying that when there were movements, troop movements, infantry troop movements in the framework of attack, the BH strategy consisted also of having support from the inside from the sniping positions, is this how I should understand your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I maintain that any clear position in clear position, that is, visible streets or any open space at Grbavica was covered by sniper fire, that is, the possibility of movement during attack. I am not talking about throughout the war, but at the time when there was an attack and the way when there were more intense or direct attacks or clashes on the lines of the defence, it was impossible to have any kind of supply of assistance, of food, throughout the territory of Grbavica because all Grbavica was covered by sniper fire which, as I said, this fire was opened from tall buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, when you say this, you are talking about military parts of Grbavica, if there were any, or civilian Grbavica, or what are you talking about specifically?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Most intense fire was directed at the lines of defence, but the sniper fire as support to the units of the BH Army was open across the territory of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know if the citizens of Grbavica had to protect themselves against this fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The exact data on civilian victims in Grbavica were never disclosed, were never made public. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you here. I will interrupt you here. Do you know if civilians in Grbavica had to protect themselves against such fire?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: How did they do this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Mostly by using screens that were set up in the street or in the streets, passages, and intersections, and these screens protected them from view facing the side of Sarajevo held by the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, earlier when I interrupted you, you were speaking about your experience in relation to the victims or the wounded. What can you tell us about this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: A certain period of time after the war, I worked at the municipality of the Serbian New Sarajevo and the service that kept a record throughout the war, I found data, a piece of data that over 1.000 -- there were over 1.000 civilian victims in that part of Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: It seems that Mr. Piletta-Zanin anticipated that answer. It is so nebulous in the foundation for that evidence as in my respectful submission to be of no assistance to the Trial Chamber. "A piece of data" --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I apologise. We don't have the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I will just -- I take it that it now is functioning again. Please proceed, Mr. Ierace. Or had you said what you intended to say? You were able to listen to the objection, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. Yes. I heard it with one ear, and I am going to reread it to make sure. Surprisingly, I didn't -- I was not anticipating this answer, but what I take note of is the following thing: Is that this witness always gave measured answers, and specific answers, and he said he worked after the war, but he did know about these facts that are in relation to the war. It doesn't matter about the period, because we are speaking about a global general number, so the fact that this witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Would you please concentrate on the core of the objection, that is that these kind of facts should not be introduced just by, I would say, if I do understand you well, Mr. Ierace, by uncontrollable data given through testimony rather than by other sources that could be controlled and are fit to -- for the other party to check. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I remember that there was testimony of an expert witness who was Mrs. Tabeau, and she was officially employed by the Prosecution who had also given data. She was also based on a kind of office, same kind of office, except that it is based on the other side of the line to the one which is opposite this witness. So is there a different kind of standard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is it the intention of the Defence to introduce what is available of those records, and then have either experts of witnesses to testify about it? Because that's how I understand the objection of Mr. Ierace, that if there is material available, that this material should be produced rather than a testimony of a witness without producing either expert reports on it or the underlying data. That's I think the issue we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I add something to my objection. I don't believe this is in the description of the witness's knowledge. Secondly, it seems from the witness's earlier reference to it on line 19 of page 78 that we are to be told that it is not available publicly. The distinction between this evidence of that of Ms. Tabeau, is that the information on which she based her conclusion was available to the Defence. It seems this is not. To suggest there were a thousand civilian victims on the Serb side, the Bosnian Serb side in Grbavica without giving any opportunity to the Prosecution to check that data, is in my respectful submission, not only inappropriate, but such as to render it inadmissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I thought that I summarised your objection approximately in this sense. Now it certainly is clear, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Could you please respond to the core of the objection which is about the possibility for the other party to check the data underlying the testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just said, but I wasn't understood correctly, is that I was surprised by this response. I did not anticipate this because I cannot tell you that this today I am going to come up from my left or my right pocket some factual proof. The only thing that I can do to enrich the Prosecution in their knowledge of facts is to tell them about the number of Serb victims during this campaign in the widest possible sense, in the city of Sarajevo, and I am speaking about the widest possible sense, a campaign. I am not talking about the legal definition of the term. Thank you very much. May I proceed, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed, but you have not yet given an answer to my question, whether the Defence intends not to tell the Prosecution what in the view of the Defence are the number of Serb victims, but whether they will produce any data which at least are fit to be investigated and to be checked on the validity of these figures. And the Prosecution has pointed out that is the difference between the approach followed by the Prosecution and now followed by the Defence. So what could we expect before we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The answer is, yes, Mr. President. The answer is yes. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, this data or completely different data, that's the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the answer is yes for the data about victims in general. So these pieces of data that I have just found out about and Mr. Ierace understood this, I am speaking about them lato sensu, not stricto sensu.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you'll understand that the -- that reliable data, controllable data, are always to be preferred. And if you intend to do so, perhaps try to find a balance between what you seek from a witness who seems not to have available at this moment this data, and what you would try to produce at later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if it is the same data, and Mr. Piletta-Zanin tells us it is, then why do we hear it from this witness, surely, given that we will be receiving it, we can wait until then and the evidence can be given then in a proper form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin tells us that he is surprised that this data does exist. But perhaps first a few questions for you. You said that there were records about the number of victims. Do you know where they are, these records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Where are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the municipality of Srpska Novo Sarajevo in an institution, in the institution of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You work with this data personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I had them, had access to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you do with them? I mean, what -- did you analyse them or did you consult them or what did you do with this data?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the first place when I discovered this data that are recorded in books, this was just a confirmation of what I had already known as to what was happening during the war in Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but my question was what you did with it. Whether it confirms your impression that's a different matter. Yes. Did you analyse it? Did you consult it and for what reason and what was the result of this activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no real analysis. There was just the factual state of affairs. So the books that I looked into, we can find those figures or rather the first and last names of people, and in most cases, also the date of their killing. And not only that, but that is not my only source of information. A source of information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I am -- whether you have other sources of information, that's perhaps for the next question. But I would first like to concentrate very much on these records. You say that these records contain names and sometimes the date when people were killed. Are these records just about people killed or also of victims being injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not the injured. I just wanted to add by way of explanation, these data, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, if it is on this data, please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Clear evidence of the number of civilian victims at Grbavica are the tombs and the inscriptions on them with the names and date of death.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got to stop you. I am asking you about the records, whether there is other evidence on the number of victims, that's a different matter, and perhaps the parties may ask you questions about that. But I am specifically interested at this moment in these records. Did I understand you well that these records indicate that some thousand people have died? Is that contained in these records?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Died and that means something else, but killed, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Killed. Please correct me if I am wrong. So that they were killed. Who did create these records? Are they medical records? Are they administrative records? Are they -- what kind of records are they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, this is done by a service attached to the municipality, and this service functioned throughout the war and kept those records.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it is an administrative recording of those killed. Does it make any distinction between whether the victims were civilians or were military people, as far as you can know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you tell us that these records are still -- if you looked at it, at these records, for what purpose, apart from perhaps that you would like to know, but was there any professional involvement in looking at it? Did you have to summarise them or did you have to extract them or did you have to copy the content of it for other purposes? Could you tell us what actually brought you to consult, at least, to look into these records? What caused you to do so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of my duties in the municipality was to cooperate with the international community. And one of the questions that were put in the course of that cooperation had to do with things that happened during the war. And this data was necessary in a certain period of time in context with a particular international institution, and that is how I found that figure, which have been verified, and which has been recorded, and I presented it during these discussions or rather contacts with the international community.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which entity of the international community are you referring to? So I do understand that this data has been provided to an international organisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is provided to any organisation from the international community if it makes such a request. And the organisations that asked me were the military forces of the international community, which is now called SFOR, in those days it was UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so this data have been provided. Was that after the war or during the war that these data were provided to the military authorities of SFOR and/or UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I was referring to was after the war. And as for the work of the municipality during the wartime, wartime I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me just confer one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now knowing better what the source of information of the witness is and how the data, according to this witness, have been distributed in the international community, the -- and also having heard that the Defence will produce the data also in other forms, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, you are allowed to ask questions about it. Of course, here again, the probative value of the information the witness gives might vary according to what other evidence will be presented in this respect and how controllable that evidence will be. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have only a few questions as the gentleman is not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: But since you spoke about that, sir, these civilians killed during those events, does one know why, how they were killed? What had provoked that death?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: With respect to civilians, in most cases it was the effect of sniper fire, which doesn't mean that they did not get killed as a result of other types of firing towards Grbavica. I am referring to shells and fire opened from other types of infantry weapons that were random.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I would like to refer to the photograph you have on the screen. And when you look at the tower in the forefront of the picture, please. Thank you. Did you hear the question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I see the building in the middle.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes. Do you see holes in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you tell us in two words what they are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: As I said, this building that we are referring to and I told you that the same applied to all the tall buildings --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No, I am just asking you what are the holes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: These holes are the results of tank fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why do you think that this type of tank fire was directed against this tower, briefly, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I object, speculation. "Why do you think tank fire was directed against this building?"

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will withdraw the words "why do you think."

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let me say: Do you know for what precise reason we see evidence of tank impact on these buildings and if yes, tell us the reason.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And what was the reason?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: It was anti-sniper fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the assistance of the usher, I should now like us to place on the ELMO our document D1811 referring to incidents 20, 15, 10, 7, et cetera. And a colour copy should be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you recognise the map on the ELMO, please; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, the lines that you see, both the light green one going northwards, as well as the darker green line going southward which could represent the positions of the armies, are those lines correct; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to the extent to which those lines are not quite correct, would you be able to draw on this map with precision the real positions of those lines; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: The Serbian lines fully, yes; as for the Muslim lines, partially.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Will you please take a black pen and in a full line redraw the Serb lines as you remember them.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, you have drawn this line. Could you please focus on the two red spots that you see in the centre of the screen and take the pointer, please, and place it slightly to the right, slightly to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: No. No. The circle in the middle, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now slightly to the right. Very lightly to the right.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, to the best of your recollection and starting from that point, the line that you continued from there, is it quite correct or wasn't there a different line starting from the section going to the left?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Roughly, as far as I can recollect, this is the continuation of the line along the road to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Were you frequently on that line?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: That is very close to where I lived, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you now please draw in a dotted line the part of the enemy line that you are familiar with.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: I am only sure of this part, that it went like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Witness, as these maps are not useful in this way for measuring distance, what is the distance between the line that you have just done, that is the dotted line of the enemy positions and point 15 marked with the number "15" on the map, what is the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: An indicator that we can use is the stadium that I am pointing to, number 217, which is some 60 metres wide. So that could be the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When you say that the stadium was 60 metres, was it 60 metres according to what you remember or is it based on what you think, viewing the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No. It is based on what I know regarding the width of a football pitch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you, was there a football pitch in that stadium?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, do you see a point number "10" on the map, and if you do could you point it out with the pointer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, my question is the following: Bearing in mind the geographic configuration of the land, could one see from the Serbian lines and taking into consideration the buildings in this area, could one see the point with the number "10"; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS DP16
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you explain why that point number 10 was not visible?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just so that I fully understand the context of the evidence, I take it that the question is intended to refer to any part of the Serbian line or any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that is what the question was about. Yes. Mr. DP16, you were answering a question on the visibility of point 10 from whatever position at the Serbian line, that's how -- that's the question you have answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the front line the answer is, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. From whatever point on the front line. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Things appear to be quite clear. We have another 10 minutes. And in view of the various, but useful interruptions, I think we could be granted a little more time. I don't think I will be abusing too much the people working in and around this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You said you would need another 10 minutes, is that how I understood you? You indicated two and a half hours for this witness, according to my bookkeeping --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Until now we have used approximately two hours and 25 minutes. So 10 minutes will be granted for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we will adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom. May I instruct you not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given or you are about to give tomorrow. And we hope to see you back tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before you adjourn, I have the CDs of C2, if I could hand those to the Registrar. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I have to adjourn again, because words spoken after we adjourned we are, in one way or another, re-opening, so we now adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 1.45 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 29th day of November, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
